headline: 12-Year-Old Repairs 114 Stuffed Animals for Fire Survivors
meta_description: Sadie Hutson of North Carolina hand-repaired 114 thrift-store stuffed animals and donated them to children who lost their homes in fires.
summary_short: A 12-year-old girl answered a community call for help by collecting and personally repairing 114 stuffed animals for children displaced by fires.
body:
A 12-year-old North Carolina girl hand-repaired 114 stuffed animals and donated them to children who lost their homes in fires. Sadie Hutson of Dubson heard the call from Disaster Program Manager Jon McCollum, who asked the community for help as home fires increased in the area and supplies ran low.

Rather than simply purchasing new toys, Hutson chose a different path: she began collecting stuffed animals from thrift stores. But collecting was only the beginning. She then repaired each of the 114 toys herself, transforming items that might otherwise have been discarded into comfort objects for families rebuilding after disaster.

Her effort shows how a young person's determination can multiply impact. By choosing repair over replacement, Hutson not only provided meaningful gifts to vulnerable children—she modeled resourcefulness and compassion for her entire community.
quick_facts: Sadie Hutson, age 12, from Dubson, North Carolina
114 stuffed animals collected from thrift stores
Each toy repaired by hand before donation
Donated to children who lost homes in fires
Inspired by community call from Disaster Program Manager
